newsitem.title: UK: Sugar freight business routine, CSR orders fixed.
newsitem.headline: Sugar freight business routine, CSR orders fixed.

text.p: Business was mostly routine on the sugar freight market at the start of the week with two first-ever orders quickly fixed, shipbrokers said on Monday. Last week, CSR quoted for tonnage for two bulk sugar shipments from Queensland to Iran and Jeddah. Market sources said both orders achieved rates in the low $20 bracket.
It issued one new inquiry for 18,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from the same origin to Japan for 10/20 November. Shipbrokers said the rate likely to be achieved was around $17.
Genoc was open for 5,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from Rouen to Algiers for early November dates.
Fiji Sugar Marketing's recent order to Japan was still open.
Mauritius Sugar Syndicate quoted for 14,500/14,750 tonnes of bulk sugar from Port Louis to London for 8/12 NOvember.
Other firmer business came from E D & F Man, said to have fully fixed 12/14,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from east coast Mexico to Colombo for 1/10 November. Details of the rate have yet to emerge.
Man also fixed 14/15,000 tonnes in bulk from Maceio or Recife to Algeria/Black Sea for the end of October.
